title: Ukraine launches nearly 500 drones at Moscow region in new large-scale attack
key_facts: Moscow's mayor Sergey Sobyanin said 493 Ukrainian drones were detected flying towards the Moscow region on the night of 14 Oct.
He said air defences intercepted another 180 as they approached the region; the Russian Ministry of Defense claimed 902 Ukrainian drones were intercepted over its territory overnight.
Moscow's four major airports suspended operations overnight because of the drone threat.
Saratov governor Roman Bursargin said one person was killed; the article reports damage near Balakovo and a Sberbank data centre under construction, with no confirmed total of impacts.
Zelenskyy said a Russian attack damaged 26 energy facilities and four oil and gas facilities and left at least 600,000 people without power.
The article says Ukraine had paused oil strikes after Trump called for an energy ceasefire, and that Zelenskyy said Russia did not follow.
quote_evidence: On October 14, Moscow’s mayor, Sergey Sobyanin, announced that 493 Ukrainian UAVs were detected flying towards the Moscow region.
The Russian Ministry of Defense claimed to have intercepted 902 Ukrainian UAVs over its territory during the night.
The attacks targeted industrial facilities and data centers across the country, but the total number of impacts has not yet been confirmed.
why_it_matters_hint: Mass drone attacks are now a routine part of the war and disrupt airports and energy supplies on both sides.
notes: Figures come from Russian officials and OSINT channels; Ukraine's own account of results not given. Opinion-led defence outlet.
